priceSnapshot.source: OKX Public API v5 /market/candles bar=4H limit=290, in-progress 16:00Z bucket, read at 12:44 COT and clock-checked before use. The /market/ticker endpoint was DISCARDED this run: it returned a well-formed payload with ts 06:42:18 COT, six hours and two minutes behind the clock, quoting 76,083.2 against a real 75,440.2.
priceSnapshot.note: Price is 75,440.2. Against the 16 September UTC open of 75,640.2 that is 200.0 points and 0.26 percent lower. Against the morning publication at 75,775.1 it is 334.9 points and 0.44 percent lower, and against the midnight print of 75,965.6 it is 525.4 points and 0.69 percent lower - three consecutive sessions each lower than the last, which has not happened since 12 September. The four hours and forty-five minutes since the morning snapshot are a single narrow slide: high 75,950.0 in the 10:00 COT hour, low 75,354.4 printed minutes ago in the 12:00 COT hour, a 595.6-point range, and price is sitting in the bottom fifteen percent of it. That low is the number that matters. The morning report set its reduce gate at 75,355.4 and required a settled 1H close beneath it. Price has now traded 75,354.4 - ONE POINT through the level - and the 12:00 COT hour is still open at 75,448.1. The gate has been tagged and not confirmed, for the fourth time in six sessions. Feed note, and this run it is a bad one: the OKX proxy served four different staleness levels inside the same two minutes. The ticker was 6.0 hours old, the 15m series was 24.0 hours old, a second 15m call was 60 days old quoting 64,153, the 5m series was 20 days old quoting 80,024, the 1D limit=250 call was 15 days old, open interest was 17.4 hours old on one call and 10 days old on another, and the long-short account ratio was 12.8 hours old on the 1H period and 2 days old on the 5m period. Every one of those was discarded. What survived the clock check and is used here: 1H candles at limit=280 (newest bucket 12:00 COT), 4H candles at limit=290 (newest bucket 11:00 COT), 1D candles at limit=220 (newest bucket 11:00 COT), the funding-rate endpoint at 11:51 COT, and the realized-liquidation tape whose newest fill is 12:43:55 COT, one minute old.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 75,354.4, the low printed in the 12:00 COT hour and now the lowest price of the session, 86.2 points under the mark. The level moves down one point from the morning's 75,355.4 because price has already been there and bought back: the gate is now the low itself rather than a level above it. The distinction the file has made money on four times this month still applies - a wick through is not a break, a settled close is. If the 13:00 COT Fed statement produces an hourly close beneath 75,354.4, the six-hour box that has held since midnight is gone, the 75,350-75,425 long-liquidation shelf underneath it becomes fuel rather than support, and the next structural level is the 74,955.5 capitulation low with nothing in between. On that close, stop adding and cut the spot core.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 76,436.6, the 1H EMA50 and the second of the four hourly averages. This is deliberately the same RULE the morning session used, re-measured rather than re-invented: the morning asked for a close above the 1H EMA50 when it sat at 76,573.6, and the average has since fallen 137.0 points to 76,436.6. The hourly stack sits 75,922.5 / 76,436.6 / 76,904.7 / 77,610.2 above price in unbroken bearish order and has not been reclaimed at any point this session. The fastest of them is only 482.3 points away and price has failed against it repeatedly, so a close above the FIRST average is noise at this range width. A settled close through the SECOND is the first evidence the stack is unwinding, and it would also clear the session high at 75,950.0 and the 75,925 short-liquidation pocket on the way.

decisionBox.changed: Position stays ADD and the tranche stays deliberately small, but the reason has narrowed to one leg from three, and that is the honest headline of this report. The morning session added because the 13 September FLUSH RULE - unbroken through six tests - had for the first time started moving the way it requires, on all three of its readings at once: open interest down 1.14 percent in an hour, the long-short account ratio down from 1.83 to 1.77, and the realized-liquidation tape inverted to 7.4-to-1 longs. This session can verify exactly ONE of those three. The liquidation leg has not just held, it has intensified: over the 09:04 to 12:43 COT window the OKX tape carried out 382,235 USD of LONGS against 28,431 USD of shorts, a 13.4-to-1 skew against the morning's 7.4-to-1, with the four heaviest clusters at 75,375, 75,425, 75,400 and 75,350 - every one of them stacked in a 75-point band directly beneath the mark. That is a long flush accelerating into support, which is what the rule wants to see. But the open-interest and account-ratio legs CANNOT BE CHECKED this run: both OKX endpoints returned stale cache, 17.4 hours and 12.8 hours behind the clock respectively, and were discarded rather than quoted. So the flush rule is not confirmed and it is also not broken - it is UNTESTED at its seventh test, and 74,955.5 remains explicitly NOT established as a flush low. One verifiable leg out of three, eight minutes before a Fed statement that is 92 percent priced for the first rate hike in three years, is a reason to keep buying small and to refuse leverage entirely. Against the add: the 10-year is at 5.01 percent having touched 5.04, the highest since July 2007; Brent is 109.21 after a 3.34 percent day on the Saudi pipeline outage; and Farside booked 450.4 million USD of spot-ETF OUTFLOWS on 15 September, the largest single-day redemption in the visible window. For it: price is still 1,709.5 points above a daily EMA50 at 73,730.7 that has not been threatened this month, 985.2 above the 4H EMA200 at 74,455.0, and the 1H MACD histogram is positive at plus 26.71 for a fifth consecutive print - though it is decaying, down from plus 79.3 at the morning publication, and that decay is why confidence falls from 6.4 to 5.8.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN and it is not close. Summing the verified tape by side of the mark: 315,400 USD of liquidation mass sits BELOW price across the 75,350 / 75,375 / 75,400 / 75,425 buckets, against 80,576 USD above it, a 3.9-to-1 imbalance downward. The nearestBelow at 75,425.0 is only 15.2 points away, which means price is not approaching the shelf - it is standing on it. Read that two ways and both are true: the shelf is why the low has been bought back four times today, and the shelf is what turns into an air pocket if a settled hourly close goes through it. The 100-fill window covers 09:04 to 12:43 COT, so it is a three-and-a-half-hour snapshot rather than a full forward book; a keyed CoinGlass heatmap would show resting orders above as well, which this free feed structurally cannot.

calibration.note: The morning's 75,355.4 reduce gate did NOT fire and the manner of its non-firing is now the most repeated pattern in this file. Price traded 75,354.4 at 12:4x COT - exactly ONE POINT through the trigger - and the 12:00 hour is open at 75,448.1, 93.7 points back above it. The gate required a settled 1H close and has not got one. That is the fourth time in six sessions the settled-close requirement has kept the wallet out of a wick, and on the three prior occasions the wick was the low. The 76,573.6 add gate did NOT fire and was never close: the best settled close since the morning was 75,789.4 at 10:00 COT, 784.2 points short, and price never traded above 75,950.0. The 74,955.5 invalidation HELD with 398.9 points of clearance. No resting stop was recommended and none was needed. On money: the morning BOUGHT a 12 USDT spot tranche at 75,775.1 and spot marks 75,440.2, so the tranche is 334.9 points and 0.44 percent offside, roughly 0.05 USDT on a 12 USDT slice. Hence false - the third consecutive small false on the discretionary line, all three of them sub-0.05 USDT, all three of them the cost of buying a range that keeps grinding lower rather than the cost of a bad rule. What did NOT resolve is the 13 September flush rule, and that is this session's real finding. The morning handed it forward with all three legs finally pointing toward a floor. This session can verify one of three: the liquidation leg, which strengthened from 7.4-to-1 to 13.4-to-1 longs. The open-interest and account-ratio legs were unreadable because both OKX endpoints served cache 17.4 and 12.8 hours old. The rule is therefore UNTESTED at its seventh test rather than passed or failed, 74,955.5 is still NOT confirmed as a flush low, and the endday session inherits an unfinished check plus whatever the 13:00 COT Fed statement does to it.
